idea.title: Carrd: one-page websites, free with a $19/year Pro plan

source.text: Carrd: one-page websites, free with a Pro plan at $19 per year, launch country US. Score it as of 2016-03-01: use only evidence published on or before that date (set verdict.as_of). Founder: a solo developer with $1,000, side project. Just go: do not ask questions. Use the slug carrd.

idea.problem: Building a simple single-page website (profile, portfolio, landing page) is slow or costly on full site builders.
idea.solution: A builder for one-page websites, free to use, with a Pro plan.
assumptions: Customer assumed: US freelancers, designers, indie makers and job seekers who need one page with a custom domain.
Pro plan assumed to include custom domains, more sites and forms.
Founder has no existing audience, template following or list.
Side project at roughly 10 hours per week.
Goal read as side income from 'side project'.
Headless run: no questions asked; scored as of 2016-03-01 with evidence published on or before that date.

confidence.note: No pre-2016 CPC for 'website builder', no dated Strikingly pricing, and no archived pricing pages; churn for $19/yr products is a benchmark.

gross_margin.note: About 90% after Stripe's $0.85 per $19 charge and hosting cents: static one-page sites are nearly free to serve.

ltv_cac.note: LTV ~$36 vs organic CAC ~$22 (estimate): 1.6. Paid search is out of reach at $19/yr.

pricing_power.note: Free tiers (Wix, Weebly, about.me) anchor near $0; $19/yr undercuts Squarespace Cover at $36/yr rather than commanding a premium.

build_effort.note: A hosted drag-and-drop builder with custom domains and SSL is 2-3 months of side-project work (estimate).

skills_match.note: Solo developer covers the build; design taste and marketing are unproven (assumption).

capital_needed.note: Hosting from $5/month and S3 at $0.03/GB: the $1,000 budget covers years of runway.

time_to_mvp.note: About 10 weeks to a paid Pro tier at side-project pace (estimate).

sales_cycle.note: A $19/year self-serve purchase is an impulse buy: no committee, same-day checkout.

channel_readiness.note: Product Hunt launches bring thousands of visitors, but the founder has no audience of their own.

search_demand.note: Wix had 77M registered users; 55% of US very small businesses still had no website in 2015.

trend.note: Wix revenue grew 43% in 2015 to $203.5M and premium subs grew 43%.

willingness_to_pay.note: People pay (1.77M Wix premium subs) but only ~2.3% of registered users convert.

free_alternatives.note: Wix, Weebly (30M sites) and about.me (5M users) do a free one-page site; R5: free alternative hit, capped at 2.

competitor_density.note: 9 competitors found incl. Squarespace Cover Pages and Strikingly; strong_competitor hit (R5 <= 3).

differentiation.note: One specific edge: price, $19/yr vs $36/yr for Squarespace Cover; the rest is simplicity.

legal_regulatory.note: Needs a DMCA agent filing and abuse handling: free subdomain hosts carried 14% of phishing in 1H2014.

platform_dependency.note: Owns the product, domain and data; relies on commodity hosting with many substitutes.

market_risk.note: Durable need: personal and small-business web presence keeps growing with mobile.

skills.note: Developer skills cover the product; no track record in design or SaaS marketing (assumption).

assets.note: No audience, list or template following stated; $1,000 only.

interest.note: Side project: curiosity, not stated domain passion (assumption).

sam.reasoning: 10% of Wix's 1.77M premium subs assumed to be single-page or personal sites = 177k x $19/yr

som.reasoning: 0.3% of SAM in year 1: ~530 Pro customers x $19/yr

price.reasoning: Founder's stated Pro price: $19 per year, billed annually

variable_cost_per_unit.reasoning: Stripe 2.9% x 19 + 0.30 = 0.85; hosting/bandwidth ~0.50; support ~0.50 per Pro user per year

churn_monthly_pct.reasoning: Mid-range of SMB SaaS churn 3-7%/month (Tunguz 2015) and 5.4% median (Point Nine 2015); annual billing pulls it lower

conversion_rate_pct.reasoning: Wix FY2015: 1.77M premium subs / 77M registered users = 2.3% free-to-paid

cac.reasoning: Launch work 40 h x $25/h = $1,000 / (2,000 free sign-ups from Product Hunt + Show HN x 2.3%) = 46 Pro users

payback_months.reasoning: CAC 21.7 / (17.15 / 12 monthly gross profit); annual upfront billing recovers $17.15 on day 1

fixed_costs_month.reasoning: $5 server (DigitalOcean 2013 price) + ~$5 storage/CDN + ~$5 domain, email, DMCA filing amortised

break_even_customers_per_month.reasoning: 15 / 1.43 monthly gross profit per Pro customer = ~11 Pro customers in total

time_to_first_revenue_weeks.reasoning: ~10 weeks of side-project build to a Pro tier with custom domains, then launch day

verdict.launch_reason: The founder's stated launch market, and home of the Product Hunt and Hacker News audiences.
verdict.cheapest_test: Landing page with 3 demo one-page sites and a $19/yr Pro pre-order button, posted to Show HN, Product Hunt and r/web_design for 7 days.
kill_criteria: Fewer than 300 waitlist sign-ups within 7 days of the Show HN / Product Hunt post -> stop
Fewer than 10 paid $19 pre-orders by day 7 -> stop
Free-to-Pro conversion below 1% after 60 days live -> stop

rescue.change: Cut scope to a 2-week MVP: fixed templates, no drag-and-drop, Pro = custom domain only, then launch on Product Hunt and Show HN
rescue.why: time_to_mvp 2 -> 4 and build_effort 2.5 -> 4: revenue in weeks, not months
rescue.requires: Discipline to ship a narrow product

rescue.change: Build distribution first: publish free one-page templates and a 'made with' badge on every free site
rescue.why: channel_readiness 2.5 -> 4 and assets 1.5 -> 3: owned, compounding channel
rescue.requires: Design skill to make templates people share

rescue.change: Niche down to one ICP (freelance designers or job seekers) with a tailored Pro bundle

type_checks.note: SMB SaaS churns 3-7%/month (Tunguz 2015); at $19/yr that caps LTV near $36, shown in ltv_cac = 2.
Targets people with no site yet; a one-page site is cheap to rebuild, so switching costs neither block entry nor protect retention.

narrative.answer: PIVOT at 64. Margins are excellent and demand is rising, but **Wix and Squarespace** already give the job away free or at $3/month, and a founder with **no audience** has only launch-day spikes to reach users.
tldr: Demand is real and rising: Wix grew revenue 43% to $203.5M in 2015.
Squarespace launched a $3/month one-page tier in Nov 2015; free tiers do the basic job.
Unit economics work at ~90% margin, but $19/yr leaves LTV near $36: only free, viral channels pay.

key_findings.title: Incumbents already sell one-page sites
key_findings.detail: Squarespace launched **Cover Pages at $3/month** in Nov 2015, backed by $78.5M raised; Wix has **77M users**.

key_findings.title: Price leaves no room for paid acquisition
key_findings.detail: At $19/yr and **3-7% monthly SMB churn**, LTV is about **$36** (estimate): only free channels can pay back.

key_findings.title: Demand rising, margins near 90%
key_findings.detail: Wix grew **43%** in 2015; serving a static page costs cents, so Stripe's **$0.85** per charge is the main cost.

narrative.recommendation: Do not build the full builder yet. Ship a 2-week, template-only MVP with a $19 Pro pre-order and launch it on Show HN and Product Hunt; continue only with 10+ pre-orders in 7 days.
narrative.steelman: Full builders are overkill for one page: a fast, ultra-simple tool at **$19/yr** (half Squarespace's $36) with ~90% margin and viral free sites can win a niche incumbents underprice. Evidence: margin and price gap hold; the channel is unproven.

premortem.cause: Launch-day traffic faded and no owned channel replaced it, so sign-ups stalled.
premortem.early_signal: Fewer than 20 organic sign-ups a day by week 3 after launch

premortem.cause: Free users never upgraded: $19/yr bought too little over free tiers.
Squarespace or Wix cut one-page pricing and out-marketed a solo founder.
premortem.early_signal: An incumbent price cut or free custom-domain offer within 30 days of launch

why_now.summary: Mobile ranking pressure and **free SSL** make cheap, responsive custom-domain pages easy to offer in early 2016, but incumbents are entering the same niche.

changes.what: Google ranks mobile-friendly pages higher on mobile search
Let's Encrypt offers free SSL certificates to anyone
64% of US adults own a smartphone, up from 35% in 2011
Squarespace prices a one-page product at $3/month, validating the segment

icp.who: US freelancers, designers, indie makers and job seekers who need one page on a custom domain
icp.pays_for_today: Squarespace Cover Page at $3/month billed annually ($36/yr), or free about.me / Wix pages
icp.budget: under $40/year (estimate, anchored by Squarespace Cover Page)
icp.trigger: Launching a side project, starting a job search or needing a link for a profile

free_alternative.evidence: Weebly (**30M** sites built), about.me (~5M users) and Wix's free plan let anyone publish a one-page site for $0 (2015).

strong_competitor.evidence: Wix: **77M** registered users and $203.5M 2015 revenue; Squarespace Cover Pages from $3/month since Nov 2015.

graveyard.evidence: Jux closed citing **slow growth** (2013); GeoCities (2009), Google Page Creator and Posterous (2013) were shut by their owners.

no_distribution.evidence: Clear: a Product Hunt feature brings **thousands** of visitors at $0; free sites can carry a viral badge. Paid search CPC before 2016 unknown.

costs_eat_margin.evidence: Clear: Stripe takes **$0.85** of $19 and a $5/month server hosts thousands of static pages: margin ~90% (estimate).

weak_demand.evidence: Clear: Wix revenue **+43%** in 2015 and 55% of US very small businesses had no website (GoDaddy, 2015).

legal_platform_risk.evidence: Clear but real work: free subdomain hosts carried **14%** of phishing attacks in 1H2014; DMCA agent filing needed for safe harbor.

saturated_wave.evidence: Clear: **6** look-alike launches found (OnePager, Resume Builder, Lead Pages, Tilda, PageCloud, Squarespace Cover Pages), under the 10 threshold.

customer.segment: US freelancers, creatives, indie makers and job seekers (assumed)
customer.pain: Full site builders are slow and priced for multi-page sites when they need one page.
customer.today: about.me or a free Wix/Weebly page on a subdomain, or Squarespace Cover Page at $36/yr

risks.risk: Phishing and spam abuse on free subdomains gets the domain blocklisted
risks.mitigation: Moderation queue, abuse reports, no free forms at first

risks.risk: Missing DMCA agent filing removes safe harbor
risks.mitigation: File the $105 designated agent form before launch

risks.risk: Incumbent price cut on one-page tiers
risks.mitigation: Stay cheaper and simpler; own a niche
Gate custom domains and badge removal behind Pro

test_plan.step: Build a landing page with 3 demo one-page sites and a $19/yr Pro pre-order via Stripe
test_plan.verify: Page live, checkout tested with 1 real charge

test_plan.step: Post Show HN and share in r/web_design and r/webdev
Launch on Product Hunt; reply to every comment
Email the waitlist the pre-order offer
Count pre-orders and interview 5 buyers about what they would use it for
test_plan.verify: 10+ pre-orders, 3+ repeat use cases -> build the 2-week MVP
